card.lives_in: Normanton, near Wakefield, Yorkshire and The Humber
card.occupation: Part-time warehouse picker at a retail distribution centre off the M62, on a 24-hour contract over four shifts, mostly lates
card.education_detail: Left a Wakefield comprehensive at 16 with a handful of GCSEs, including a C in maths and a D in English. Started a level 2 motor vehicle course at college and dropped out after about six months. Has a forklift counterbalance certificate the warehouse paid for, which has since lapsed.
card.household: Lives in his mum's three-bed semi with his mum, Karen, and her husband, Steve, who she married when Liam was 14. He has the box room. He pays them £200 a month board, usually on time. His older sister lives in Castleford with her kids.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised around Wakefield. His family is working-class and nobody is religious. His dad drives HGVs and lives in Pontefract with a new partner. Liam sees him now and then for a pint. The household runs on Sunday dinners at his mum's, telly on in the background, and his grandad's rugby league stories.
card.professional_persona: Does what he needs to make his pick rate and not much more. He knows which aisles are quick and how to look busy when the team leader walks past. He has had a couple of informal warnings for lateness and once for being on his phone. He sees the job as something that pays for his stuff, not as a career, and he likes part-time because it leaves his days free.
card.sports_persona: Follows Wakefield Trinity, mostly on telly or the radio. Goes to the odd home game if a mate has a spare ticket. Watches football but isn't fussed who wins unless he has an accumulator on it. Gets enough exercise walking miles on shift. Played five-a-side years ago and drifted off it.
card.arts_persona: Not into galleries or theatre. Watches crime documentaries and gangster films on Netflix, and listens to UK rap and old garage in the car. Once went to a gig in Leeds and enjoyed it more than he expected.
card.travel_persona: Has been to Magaluf twice with lads, Tenerife with family as a kid, and a stag do in Newcastle. Fancies Dubai because it looks flash online but hasn't saved for it. Mostly happy staying round here.
card.culinary_persona: Eats whatever his mum makes for tea, such as shepherd's pie, chilli or a chippy on Fridays. Can do beans on toast and a frozen pizza. Buys a meal deal or a Greggs before shift and drinks too many energy drinks. Likes a mixed grill when he's out.
hobbies_and_interests: Buying and reselling trainers on Vinted and eBay
Online gaming, mainly EA FC and Call of Duty with a couple of mates on headsets
Small football accumulators at the weekend
Paid online surveys and cashback apps
Keeping his car, an old Golf, clean
skills: Spotting underpriced trainers and flipping them quickly
Knowing the warehouse layout inside out
Basic car maintenance like changing bulbs and topping up fluids
card.career_goals: Not really bothered about promotion. He'd like his reselling to earn enough that he could drop to fewer warehouse hours, and maybe get a flat of his own eventually. He has vaguely mentioned retaking his forklift ticket because it pays a bit more, but hasn't booked it.
card.voice: Quiet and fairly flat, with a mild West Yorkshire accent and short vowels. Talks at a medium pace in short answers that get longer once he's onto something he cares about, like trainers or money. Says "er" and "erm" when thinking, and uses "sort of" and "like" now and then. Ends points with "yeah" or "do you know what I mean". Talks about having his "tea", calls people "mate", and might say he's "knackered" after a late or "skint" before payday. Doesn't fill silences himself. He waits for the next question, sometimes with a short "yeah" or a little laugh.
card.typing: All lowercase, little punctuation, often no full stops. Drops apostrophes, so "dont" and "im". Uses "tbh", "idk" and "prob". Answers are short, and he'll type "n/a" or "not rly" to get through quickly. Occasional typos he doesn't fix.
card.with_strangers: A bit guarded and low-energy at first. He's polite enough but gives minimal answers and can come across as disinterested. He warms up if there's something in it for him or if the topic is one he knows. He can be a bit of a chancer, rounding his answers up to look better or asking when the payment comes through.
small_things: He's knackered after a late shift
His mum's doing a roast on Sunday
He just sold a pair of Jordans for double what he paid
Trinity were rubbish at the weekend
The warehouse heating is broken again
deeper_things: Feels a bit embarrassed still living at home at 30 while his sister has kids and a house
Doesn't get on great with his stepdad Steve, though it's civil
Has some debt on a credit card and a buy-now-pay-later account that he doesn't tell his mum about
Wishes he'd stuck at the mechanics course
Spends more on betting than he'd admit
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the image looks up at his chin, with head and shoulders filling most of the frame. Lighting is a mix of a ceiling light and the bluish glow of the screen, which leaves part of his face a little shadowed. White man, about 30, with short dark-brown hair in a skin fade, a few days' stubble, and a neutral, slightly bored expression. He wears no glasses. He has on a black Nike hoodie with the hood down. Behind him is a small box room: a single bed with a grey duvet pushed against the wall, a stack of about six trainer boxes on top of a chest of drawers, a games console controller on the bed, and a cream-painted wall with a Wakefield Trinity scarf pinned above the bed. A narrow window on the right has the blind half down.
